Named unary ops written by precedence (issue 01a1690b-1d10). Canon writes a
named unary bare where the source wrote it bare, with its call parens where
the source wrote `NAME(` (the ArgParen flag) or where the operator after it
is tighter than a named unary. Each snippet's Deparse,-p is perl 5.44.0's.

=== defined before a looser or
defined $x || $y;
--- facts
faithful
# (defined($x) or $y);

=== ref before eq
ref $x eq 'A';
--- facts
faithful
# (ref($x) eq 'A');

=== defined under not
!defined $x;
--- facts
faithful
# not(defined($x));

=== lc at a right operand
$a . lc $b;
--- facts
faithful
# ($a . lc($b));

=== chdir with a filetest modifier
chdir 't' if -d 't';
--- facts
faithful
# chdir('t') if (-d 't');

=== shift with no operand
shift;
--- facts
faithful
# shift(@ARGV);

=== filetest with an operand
-e $f;
--- facts
faithful
# (-e $f);

=== defined with the source's call parens
defined($x) || $y;
--- facts
faithful
# (defined($x) or $y);

=== exists on a hash element
exists $h{a};
--- facts
faithful
# exists $h{'a'};

=== defined absorbs a tighter power
defined $x ** 2;
--- facts
faithful
# defined(($x ** 2));

=== defined keeps its parens before a tighter power
defined($x) ** 2;
--- facts
faithful
# (defined($x) ** 2);

=== defined with a space before its call parens
defined ($x) . "a";
--- facts
faithful
# (defined($x) . 'a');

=== a visible unary prototype
sub one($){1} one $x, 2;
--- facts
faithful
# (one($x), '???');

=== a builtin unary import
use builtin qw(blessed); blessed $o, 1;
--- facts
faithful
# (builtin::blessed($o), '???');

=== method names are not named unaries
$o->shift(1); $o->keys;
--- facts
faithful
# $o->shift(1); $o->keys;

=== pos as an assignment target
pos $s = 1;
--- facts
faithful
# (pos($s) = 1);

=== ord absorbs a shift
ord $x << 2;
--- facts
faithful
# ord(($x << 2));

=== lc absorbs a binding match
lc $x =~ /a/;
--- facts
match 1 exact
faithful
# lc(($x =~ /a/));

=== a unary plus before a parenthesised operand is not call parens
defined +($x) . 1;
--- facts
faithful
# defined(($x . '1'));

=== a named unary as a hash key is a string
$h{shift};
--- facts
faithful
# $h{'shift'};

=== shift with no operand before a concatenation
$x = shift . 1;
--- facts
faithful
# ($x = shift(@ARGV) . '1');

=== lc of a niladic plus one
lc time + 1;
--- facts
faithful
# lc((time + 1));

=== an optional-argument prototype before an or
sub h(;$){1} h || 1;
--- facts
faithful
# (h() or '???');

=== a user sub overriding a named unary is a list operator
use subs 'chdir'; chdir $x, 1;
--- facts
faithful
# main::chdir($x, 1);
# psc reads chdir here as the builtin named unary, (chdir($x), 1): a tree
# defect `faithful` cannot see, because canon writes the source's spelling
# either way. Reported with issue 01a1690b-1d10's review.

=== a forward declaration after a list-prototype body
sub g(@){1} sub g($); $r = g $x, $y;
--- facts
faithful
# Prototype mismatch: sub g (@) vs ($); ($r = g($x, $y));

=== a forward declaration after a unary-prototype body
sub g($){1} sub g(@); $r = g $x, $y;
--- facts
faithful
# Prototype mismatch: sub g ($) vs (@); (($r = g($x)), $y);
